summary: Fixes SEC-21.5-01 (MEDIUM) from the task 21.5 release security review: the four named provider HTTP clients no longer follow HTTP redirects, so the X-Api-Key header applied by SecretLease.ApplyTo is sent only on the request to the configured connection. ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.RegisterProviderHttpClients now configures a primary handler for all four names (strict Sonarr/Radarr through the new CreateStrictHandler with AllowAutoRedirect=false; both .Insecure names through the existing CreateInsecureHandler, which keeps DangerousAcceptAnyServerCertificateValidator and adds the same AllowAutoRedirect=false), so the opt-in TLS relaxation changes certificate validation only and cannot widen credential scope; pooling and the DI shape are unchanged and no dependency was added. SonarrClient.ClassifyStatus and RadarrClient.ClassifyStatus gained an explicit >=300 and <400 arm that fails closed as the bounded InvalidResponse provider error with ArrErrorRetryability.Never and a fixed message naming the redirect and suggesting base-URL verification; no response body, header value, Location value, or secret can reach it, and the transient retry count/backoff are unchanged (a redirect is not re-sent as a retryable transient). New tests/ArrTags.Tests/ProviderRedirectTransportTests.cs adds 10 cases over two loopback origins and the real registration: a 302 redirect theory for all four named clients asserting the second origin receives nothing while the configured origin receives exactly one key-bearing request; a registration-shape test asserting all four names have redirect-following disabled, the two .Insecure names keep the relaxed certificate callback, and the strict names do not; a positive control that a healthy probe sends the unchanged X-Api-Key header; and a retry-bound control (503 with TransientRetryCount=1 yields exactly 2 requests). Pre-fix probes: all four restored to the old bare AddHttpClient shape -> Failed 5 / Passed 5 / Total 10 (4 redirect cases fail with Assert.Empty on the second origin, registration case fails with an empty action list); only the insecure handler left pre-fix -> Failed 3 / Passed 7 / Total 10 (both .Insecure redirect cases and the registration case, on 'ArrTags.Sonarr.Insecure must not follow redirects'). Both probes were reverted and the focused class passes 10/10. Documentation: the constraint is recorded in docs/architecture/07-sonarr-and-radarr-integration.md and docs/architecture/11-failure-consistency-and-security-policy.md, as an implementation note in docs/decisions/ADR-005.md (no amendment, so docs/decisions/00-index.md is unchanged), and in docs/changelog/v1.2.0.md; PLANS.md ticks 21.7 and docs/plan/state.json records it done with this report. Transport-only: no golden, RenderVersion, renderer-schema, configuration, or dependency change.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a provider origin that answers 302 with a Location naming a different origin, the plugin issues no request to that other origin, and the X-Api-Key value is never sent to it.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: tests/ArrTags.Tests/ProviderRedirectTransportTests.cs::ProviderRedirectIsNotFollowedAndTheKeyNeverReachesTheTarget runs for strict and insecure-TLS Sonarr and Radarr against two loopback origins, uses the real registrator DI, ArrHttpClientFactory, and client, and asserts Assert.Empty(target.Requests) after the 302 (with the configured origin receiving exactly one request carrying 'X-Api-Key: sec-21-5-01-transport-secret'). Pre-fix probe A is the discriminating counter-case: the second origin recorded 'GET /collect HTTP/1.1' and the assertion failed.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: All four named provider clients (strict Sonarr, strict Radarr, and both opt-in insecure-TLS clients) are registered with redirect-following disabled; a registration that drops the setting fails a test.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: tests/ArrTags.Tests/ProviderRedirectTransportTests.cs::AllFourNamedProviderClientsForbidRedirectsAndKeepTheirTlsPolicy resolves the real HttpClientFactoryOptions for ArrTags.Sonarr, ArrTags.Radarr, ArrTags.Sonarr.Insecure, and ArrTags.Radarr.Insecure, runs the registered handler-builder actions, and asserts FollowsRedirects(primary) is false for each; probe A (bare AddHttpClient shape) fails it with 'Assert.NotEmpty() Failure: Collection was empty', and probe B (insecure handler only) fails it on 'ArrTags.Sonarr.Insecure must not follow redirects'. Source: ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.RegisterProviderHttpClients configures all four names and both handlers set AllowAutoRedirect=false.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The opt-in insecure-TLS relaxation still works for its intended purpose and does not re-enable redirect-following or change the header the plugin sends.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The registration-shape test asserts the two .Insecure handlers still carry ServerCertificateCustomValidationCallback (the dangerous validator retained by CreateInsecureHandler) and that the strict handlers do not, alongside AllowAutoRedirect=false on all four. The redirect theory and ConfiguredProviderOriginReceivesTheApiKeyHeader execute the real .Insecure clients and observe the identical 'X-Api-Key' header (key absent from the request line) that the strict clients send.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A not-followed 3xx surfaces as a bounded provider error containing no secret, no response body, no header value, and no Location value, and the configured retry bound is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The redirect theory asserts ArrProviderErrorCode.InvalidResponse, ArrErrorRetryability.Never, message length <= ArrProviderError.MaxMessageLength, the message mentions the redirect, and the message contains neither the API key, nor the response-body sentinel, nor the response-header sentinel, nor the target Location URL. The same case configures TransientRetryCount=2 and the configured origin receives exactly one request, so the redirect is terminal; TransientServerErrorStillUsesTheConfiguredRetryBound configures TransientRetryCount=1 and a 503 origin receives exactly two key-bearing requests, proving the retry path and bound are intact. Source: the explicit >=300 and <400 arm in both ClassifyStatus methods.

interpretations.question: How a not-followed 3xx is surfaced, since the task delegated the decision but fixed its bounds (bounded provider error through the existing ArrProviderError/ClassifyStatus path, no secret/body/header/Location, retry bound unchanged, not re-sent as a retryable transient).
interpretations.chosen: An explicit >=300 and <400 arm in both clients' ClassifyStatus maps the redirect to ArrProviderErrorCode.InvalidResponse with ArrErrorRetryability.Never and the fixed message 'The provider answered with a redirect, which is not followed; verify the configured base URL.'
interpretations.basis: The task's work item explicitly delegates the surfacing decision within those bounds; matching the pre-existing generic arm (unmatched non-success statuses already mapped to InvalidResponse/Never) keeps the code, health mapping, and retry semantics identical while making the redirect diagnosable and the decision code-owned. The message is a code-owned literal, never provider-controlled text.
interpretations.impact: Operator-visible only: a provider that answers 3xx now reports this specific bounded message instead of the generic 'The provider returned an unexpected response status.' (same code, health, and retryability). No persisted state, configuration, or retry bound changes.

interpretations.question: Which primary-handler type to use for the strict clients (HttpClientHandler with AllowAutoRedirect=false versus SocketsHttpHandler).
interpretations.basis: The .NET client factory's default primary handler is HttpClientHandler, so using the same type preserves every other default (proxy, cookies, automatic decompression) and changes only redirect-following; the task permits either mechanism.
interpretations.impact: None observable; transport behaviour differs only in redirect-following.

test_sensitivity: Probe A: with all four registrations temporarily restored to the pre-fix shape (bare AddHttpClient for strict, insecure handler without AllowAutoRedirect), the focused class is Failed 5 / Passed 5 / Total 10. The four redirect cases fail on Assert.Empty() with the second origin's recorded 'GET /collect' request (the leak SEC-21.5-01 describes), and the registration case fails on an empty handler-action list. The passing five are the positive controls and the retry-bound case, which do not depend on the fix.

Probe B: with only the two strict clients fixed and the insecure handler temporarily pre-fix, the focused class is Failed 3 / Passed 7 / Total 10: both .Insecure redirect cases fail and the registration case fails on 'ArrTags.Sonarr.Insecure must not follow redirects'. This proves the insecure path cannot regress independently.

Both probes were reverted (cp of the saved fixed file) and 'git diff' is the intended change only; the post-fix focused run is Failed 0 / Passed 10 / Total 10. The full suites (default, host-guarded, forced-native) were run on the final restored tree.

Negative-control bound: the redirect theory's second-origin observation uses a 250 ms bounded period; a followed hop completes inside SendAsync before the probe returns, so the period is a scheduler grace rather than a race window, and no request can arrive afterwards because the client has completed the call.

A provider or reverse proxy that legitimately issues a 3xx (for example an http-to-https or trailing-slash redirect) now fails closed as a bounded provider error instead of being followed. This is the intended behavior of the fix and is documented in the architecture sections and the changelog so an operator can diagnose it; it is not silently swallowed.
